Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.  In this petition after extensive hearing, this Court had passed a detailed order on 10th March 2026, indicating that in view of the material on record, the petition ought to be allowed.

But,
effective order could not be passed because of a genuine difficulty faced by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3-National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in the form of a particular document not having been served, which was part of the documents filed with the writ petition.

The said document is at Exhibit 'F', being a map drawn by the Competent Authority of the State i.e. the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records, which has a bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc crucial bearing on the claims made by the petitioners.
In that light, it was directed that the copy of the same shall be served upon the respondent No.3-NHAI and an opportunity was granted to the said respondent to file an additional affidavit.

sentences.text: Today, when the petition is called out for hearing, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3-NHAI submits that a scanned copy of the additional affidavit has been forwarded to him by the said respondent, while the original is in transit.
A copy is tendered for perusal of this Court.
The same is taken on record.
The respondent No.3-NHAI is directed to file the original sworn affidavit on record of this petition, within one week from today.
4. We again extensively heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned AGP for the respondent Nos.1 and 2 and the learned counsel representing the respondent No.3-NHAI.
5. The petitioners are agriculturists and owners of land located in Gat Nos.46/2 and 46/3 of Village Dodi Khurd, Tal. Sinnar, Dist. Nashik.
The petitioners state that part of their lands located in the said Gat numbers were utilized for construction of the Khed Sinnar section of National Highway No.50 (NH 50).

The petitioners further state that, although final award dated 30 th October 2013 was passed, determining monetary compensation payable to the petitioners to the extent of 900 sq.
mtrs. of their land, much more land was utilized for construction of the said highway.
bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc 6.

It is brought to our notice that immediately after the said award was rendered, on 26th December 2013, the petitioner No.1 submitted a representation before the respondent Nos.2 i.e. the Competent Authority for acquisition of land for the national highway, stating that there was lack of clarity as regards the land utilized for construction of the highway and therefore, appropriate request was made on behalf of the petitioner No.1.
7.

It appears that on the representation made by the petitioners dated 14th February 2014, the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records addressed communication to the petitioner No.1 about proposed measurement of the land, which would clarify as to the extent of land of the petitioners utilized for construction of the said highway.
Thereupon, the exercise was undertaken and this is also evident from a further communication dated 31 st August 2015 on record.

Along with the said communication, a map was forwarded to the petitioners, stating that 0.25 Are (2500 sq. mtrs.) of land of petitioner No.1 from Gat No.46/2 and 0.14 Are (1400 sq. mtrs.) of land of petitioner No.2 from Gat No.46/3 was utilized for construction of the highway.

8. At exhibit 'F' with the petition is a map confirming the said facts and it records that the measurement was undertaken on the basis of an order dated 12th July 2016 passed by the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition).

The said document also shows a corrected joint measurement description, reiterating the utilization of total 3900 sq. mtrs. of land belonging to the petitioners for bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc construction of the highway.
It is significant to note that the representative of the Department of Land Acquisition also signed the said document.

9. Along with the writ petition, a document is placed on record at Exhibit 'G', which is a letter dated 27 th September 2018 addressed by the Deputy Superintendent of the Land Records to the respondent No.2 i.e. Competent Authority for Land Acquisition for National Highways, clearly stating that 0.39 Are equal to 3900 sq. mtrs. of land from Gat No.46 was utilized for construction of Zumbarabai Hari Avhad vs The State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106061416/
2 the highway.

10. In this backdrop, the petitioners sent representations to the respondent-State Authorities,
including representation dated 21 st February 2023, seeking compensation for the additional area utilized for construction of the highway beyond 900 sq. mtrs.
As there was no response, the petitioners were constrained to file this writ petition.

11. The respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed their reply affidavit and stated that specific communications dated 2 nd November 2023 and 22nd January 2025 were addressed by respondent No.2 to the Project Director of the NHAI with respect to the aforementioned aspect of the extent of land utilized for construction of the highway.
12. The respondent No.3-NHAI in its reply affidavit as well as the additional affidavit has simply denied the claims of the bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc petitioners.

It is stated that according to the record available with the said respondent and on the basis of documents concerning the aforementioned land acquisition award, only 900 sq. mtrs. was utilized and compensation had been duly determined and paid to the petitioners.
13. The learned counsel for the petitioners relied upon the aforementioned documents in respect of the prayer made in the present writ petition.

The reply affidavit of respondent Nos.1 and 2 does indicate the said position that came on record upon joint measurement undertaken by the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records was brought to the notice of the respondent No.3-NHAI.

But,
today, the learned AGP submitted that it appeared that after the award was rendered, certain officers of the State, were entertaining such applications for joint measurement, leading to the relief claimed by persons like the petitioners herein.

It was submitted that in terms of the statutory scheme of the National Highways Act, 1956, the petitioners, at the relevant time, had opportunity to raise their objections and therefore, they cannot make a grievance.
14. The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3-NHAI made submissions in line with the affidavits filed before this Court.
15. We have considered the rival submissions in the light of the material on record.

We find that this is a case where the petitioner No.1, despite being an agriculturist and a lady, had expressed her bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc concern almost immediately after the land acquisition award dated 30th October 2013 was rendered in the present case.
It is undisputed that the award determines monetary compensation as regards acquisition of land belonging to the petitioners, only to the extent of 900 sq. mtrs.

It would have been a different matter if the representations made by the petitioners immediately after the award being rendered had not resulted in any concrete material coming on record to support the assertion made on their behalf.

We have already noted hereinabove the documents filed on record with the writ petition, including communications addressed by the Deputy Superintendent of Land Record to the petitioners as well as respondent No.2-Competent Authority, confirming the fact that total 3900 sq. mtrs. of land was utilized for construction of the highway.

It is relevant to note that the corrected joint measurement report at Exhibit 'F' along with the map bears the signature of the officer of the Land Acquisition Department and as a matter of Zumbarabai Hari Avhad vs The State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 26 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106061416/
3 fact, exercise of joint measurement was undertaken by the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records on the basis of an order dated 12th July 2016 passed by the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition).
16.

sentences.text: It is also relevant to note that the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records had specifically communicated on 27 th September 2018 to the respondent No.2-Competent Authority for land acquisition that 0.39 Are equal to 3900 sq. mtrs. of land in Survey No. 46 had been utilized for the Khed Sinnar section of NH 50.
bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc 17.

In the affidavit in reply, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have also referred to and annexed communications dated 2nd November 2023 and 22nd January 2025 sent to the respondent No.3-NHAI on the aforesaid issue.

18. In the face of such material and the fact that the petitioners pursued the matter immediately after the land acquisition award was rendered, indicate that sufficient material was on record to demonstrate that while compensation was determined only for 900 sq. mtrs. of land belonging to the petitioners in Gat No.46, total land to the extent of 3900 sq. mtrs. was utilized.

This clearly indicates that the petitioners have been deprived of compensation in accordance with law for the additional 3000 sq. mtrs. of their land utilized for the purpose of the respondent No.3-NHAI.
19.

The denials of respondent No.3-NHAI, primarily based on the contents of the land acquisition award dated 30 th October 2013, cannot be of any avail in the facts and circumstances of the present case and the material placed on record.

We also do not accept the contention raised on behalf of respondents that the petitioners had ample opportunity as per the scheme of the National Highways Act, 1956 to raise appropriate objections at the relevant time.

20. The nature of objections raised by the petitioners could have been raised only after the award was rendered, for the reason that utilization beyond 900 sq. mtrs. came to light only after the exercise of joint measurement undertaken by the officers of the bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc State itself, including the Deputy Superintendent of Land Records, after the award was passed, on the basis of representations made by the petitioners.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 cannot be permitted to take a stand beyond the contents of their reply affidavit filed in the present writ petition.
21. We also find that in the additional affidavit tendered on behalf of respondent No.3-NHAI, there are only bald denials and reliance is placed on the award.
But, there is no worthwhile response given to the cogent material placed on record on behalf of the petitioners in support of their contentions.
22. We are satisfied that the petitioners have made out a case in their favour for granting reliefs in terms of prayers made in the present writ petition.

23. In view of the above, the writ petition is allowed in terms of prayer clauses (a) and (b), which read as follows :

sentences.text: "a] This Hon'ble Court may by appropriate writ, direction and order, may be pleased to hold and declare that the action of taking possession of the excess portion of the land admeasuring about 0 H. 30 R from Gat No. 46 owned by the Petitioners without following the due process of law is illegal and bad in law.

b] This Hon'ble Court may further be pleased to direct the Respondents to pass a fresh Award in respect of the land admeasuring about 0 H. 30 R from Gat No. 46 [Gat No.46/2 admeasuring about 0 H. 08 R Gat No.46/3 which is admeasuring about 0 H. 22 R] by following the procedure as prescribed under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956."
bipin prithiani 904-wp-14155.23.doc 24.

The respondents shall take immediate steps to acquire the additional 3000 sq. mtrs. land of the petitioners in Gat Nos.46/2 and 46/3, in accordance with law, and the process shall be completed within a period of one year from today.
25. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
